lesson_title: Gold to the Coast, Beads to the Hill
hook_text: A glass bead from India and a piece of Chinese pottery, found deep in Limpopo. How did they get there?
clip_script: Thohoyandou, string on a floor map. From Mapungubwe, porters walk hundreds of kilometres to the coast, carrying gold and ivory on their heads and shoulders. At Sofala, traders load them onto dhows. The monsoon winds carry the ships to Arabia, India and beyond. Back come glass beads, cotton cloth and even Chinese porcelain. Africa, Arabia, India and China, linked by trade, about eight hundred years ago. An early kind of globalisation.
visual_style: Whiteboard floor map with string lines stretching from Mapungubwe to Sofala, then across the Indian Ocean, dhows with triangular sails moving along them.
mood: Adventurous and wide, like following a long journey.
pacing: Slow walk to the coast, a quick sea crossing with the winds, then goods flowing back.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and trace the trade route from Mapungubwe to India on a map.
